# Market Juice

> Market Juice is a free daily market-literacy digest for kids ages 10-16. Each morning a short digest (about 3 minutes) explains what the stock market did and why, in kid-friendly language, with three games that each teach one of 11 core investing principles. Parents sign their kids up; it is education, not financial advice.

## Key facts

- Price: 100% free. No subscription, no upsells, no paywalls, no ads.
- Audience: kids ages 10-16. Parents sign up; for kids 12 and under, a parent must give consent by email before the account turns on (COPPA).
- Time: about 3 minutes a day.
- Schedule: a new digest is published every morning at 7 AM Eastern, seven days a week. Most editions cover the previous trading day; Sunday's edition wraps up the past week and Monday's previews the week ahead.
- What's in a digest: a market scoreboard (S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow), the biggest mover (or a company to watch), two or three kid-friendly news stories, a "did you know" fact, a word of the day, and a daily challenge of three games, plus a guess-the-company puzzle (Mystery Mover).
- Progress: kids earn pretend Market Coins, keep streaks, and climb ranks from Rookie to Wall Street Legend. No real money or brokerage account is involved.
- How content is made: each digest is drafted by AI from real market data and current news, then passes automated checks (kid-safe language filter, strict format validation, puzzle guardrails) before publishing. Company spotlights come from a hand-picked list of 75 companies kids recognize. New glossary terms go live only after human approval. A published digest never changes.
- Privacy: collects very little: the parent's email, the kid's first name and age, login credentials, game progress, and a few technical details such as timezone and the signup IP address (kept for COPPA consent records). No data selling, no ads, no training AI on kids' data; parents can delete everything at any time.

## The 11 investing principles

1. Pay Yourself First: save before you spend.
2. Compound Growth: make your money work for you.
3. Wealth Is the Gap: spend less than you earn.
4. Know What You Own: invest in what you understand.
5. Diversify: don't put all your eggs in one basket.
6. Be Patient: think in years, not days.
7. Control Your Emotions: don't follow the crowd.
8. Think Like an Owner: a share is a slice of a real business.
9. Stay Consistent: regular investing beats perfect timing.
10. Price vs Value: the price is what you pay; value is what you get.
11. Own Assets: own things that pay you.
